# SystemInfo

What [`GetSystemInfo`](/docs/api/windows/system-info#get-system-info) reports about the machine.

```rux
pub struct SystemInfo {
    pub pageSize: uint32;
    // private fields
}
```

The two granularities are not the same and the difference matters: `pageSize` is what protection is applied at,
while `allocationGranularity` is what a reservation's base address is rounded to, and on every Windows release it
is 64 KiB rather than a page. A reservation therefore wastes address space that a page-granular system would not.

## Fields

| Name       | Type     | Description                                                        |
| ---------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pageSize` | `uint32` | The size of a page, which is what memory protection is applied at. |

## Related

<h3 id="get-system-info"><code>GetSystemInfo</code></h3>

```rux
pub extern func GetSystemInfo(info: *var SystemInfo)
```

Reads what the system reports about the machine, including its page size.
Cannot fail and reports nothing: the structure is always filled.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getsysteminfo](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getsysteminfo)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Kernel.rux#L195)

**Parameters**
